sourceNote: Core sites from Wikipedia Geosearch API. Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Lotus Temple, Akshardham, Lodi Garden, Hauz Khas Village, Dilli Haat and Rashtrapati Bhavan added as curated from Wikipedia. All records needs_review.

places.name: Red Fort
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site, the main residence of Mughal emperors from 1648 to 1857. Red sandstone walls enclose the Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Rang Mahal and museum galleries. Site of India's Independence Day address every August 15. ASI-managed; budget 2 hours.

places.name: Qutub Minar
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — India's tallest brick minaret at 73m, completed in the early 13th century. The complex also contains the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque ruins, the Iron Pillar of Delhi (a 4th-century metallurgical marvel resistant to corrosion), and several tombs. Budget 90 minutes.

places.name: Humayun's Tomb
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — the first Mughal garden-tomb in India (1572), which served as the architectural inspiration for the Taj Mahal. Double-domed structure in red sandstone with white marble inlay, set in a formal charbagh (four-part) garden. Usually less crowded than Red Fort; exceptional architectural photography site.

places.name: Jama Masjid
places.description: India's largest mosque, built 1644–1658 by Shah Jahan, accommodating 25,000 worshippers. Red sandstone and white marble; three gateways with minarets 40m high. Non-Muslims can enter except during prayer times. Minaret climb available (separate fee). Adjacent to Chandni Chowk food streets.

places.name: Lotus Temple
places.description: Bahai House of Worship shaped like a blooming lotus flower, completed in 1986. Open to all religions for silent meditation and prayer; no services or rituals conducted. One of the most visited buildings in the world. No photography inside; impressive exterior architecture. Silent queue system on busy days.

places.name: Chandni Chowk
places.description: One of the oldest and busiest street markets in Delhi, dating from the 17th century Mughal era. The main boulevard runs from Red Fort to Fatehpuri Mosque. Specialist bazaars for spices (Khari Baoli), books (Nai Sarak), electronics, fabrics, and wedding supplies. Iconic street food at Paranthe Wali Gali and Ghantewala.

places.name: India Gate
places.description: 42m war memorial arch at the centre of New Delhi's ceremonial boulevard (Kartavya Path), dedicated to 70,000 Indian soldiers who died in WWI. Surrounded by large lawns popular for evening walks. The Eternal Flame (Amar Jawan Jyoti) was originally housed here. Best visited at dusk when the arch is illuminated.

places.name: Akshardham Temple, Delhi
places.description: Vast Hindu temple complex on the Yamuna bank, inaugurated in 2005. The main mandir features 234 ornately carved pillars and 20,000 sculptures with no steel or concrete. Exhibitions, a boat ride and water show are also on-site. No phones or cameras permitted inside. Plan 3–4 hours for the full experience.

places.name: Lodi Garden
places.description: 90-acre landscaped park containing 15th-century Lodi and Sayyid dynasty tombs including Mohammed Shah's Tomb, Sikander Lodi's Tomb and Bara Gumbad. Popular morning jogging circuit with 100+ bird species recorded. One of Delhi's best spaces for a peaceful morning walk; free entry.

places.name: Hauz Khas Village
places.description: Medieval reservoir complex from the 14th century surrounded by boutique cafes, galleries and fashion stores in renovated havelis. The Hauz Khas Fort and madrasa overlook a large lake with deer. Popular with Delhi's young creative crowd. Best in the afternoon for shopping and cafes; evening for rooftop bars.
places.openingDays: Shops typically 11:00–21:00; historical complex open all day

places.name: National Museum of India
places.description: India's largest museum with over 200,000 objects spanning 5,000 years, including Harappan civilisation artefacts, Gandhara sculptures, decorative arts and pre-historic tools. Takes 2–3 hours to explore selectively. Well-labelled exhibits; audio guides available. On Janpath opposite India Gate.

places.name: Dilli Haat
places.description: Permanent open-air craft market near INA Metro station with rotating stalls representing all Indian states. Artisans sell textiles, handicrafts, jewellery, ceramics and food from their regions. Good for authentic state-specific purchases. Small entry fee; spend 1–2 hours browsing.

places.name: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib
places.description: Historic Sikh gurdwara in Chandni Chowk marking the site where Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, was executed on Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb's orders in 1675. Free community langar (meals) served daily to all. No photography inside; modest dress required.

places.name: Nizamuddin Dargah
places.description: Sufi shrine of 14th-century mystic Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya in a dense neighbourhood near Humayun's Tomb. Famous for its Thursday-evening qawwali (Sufi devotional music) which draws large crowds. Narrow lanes, no photography near the dargah. Free entry; offerings accepted.
places.openingDays: Open all day; qawwali Thursday evenings after Maghrib

places.name: Kartavya Path (Rajpath)
places.description: New Delhi's ceremonial boulevard running 3km from India Gate to Rashtrapati Bhavan, redesigned in 2022. Lined with vast lawns, reflecting pools and canopied pathways. Site of the Republic Day parade every January 26. Pleasant evening walk; free access. Renamed from Rajpath to Kartavya Path in September 2022.

places.name: Partition Museum, Delhi
places.description: Museum documenting the 1947 Partition of India through personal testimonies, photographs and artefacts. Located in Town Hall, Old Delhi. Complements a visit to Chandni Chowk and Red Fort by providing historical depth. Budget 1.5 hours for a meaningful experience.

places.name: National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi
places.description: India's premier modern and contemporary art museum in Jaipur House, a former royal residence. Collection includes works by Rabindranath Tagore, Amrita Sher-Gil and other seminal Indian artists. Well-presented permanent collection; rotating temporary exhibitions. Budget 90 minutes.

places.name: National War Memorial
places.description: India's national war memorial inaugurated in 2019, honouring soldiers fallen post-Independence. Located just behind India Gate on the hexagonal complex of Kartavya Path. Features the Eternal Flame (Amar Jawan Jyoti, moved here from India Gate in 2022), bronze sculptures and granite walls inscribed with 25,942 names. Free entry.

places.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
places.description: 100-acre park adjacent to Qutub Minar complex containing 80+ medieval monuments scattered through a forested area. Features tombs, mosques, baolis (stepwells) and pavilions from the 10th–18th centuries. Less visited than Qutub Minar itself; rewarding for heritage enthusiasts who want to explore off the beaten track.

places.name: Karim's Restaurant, Old Delhi
places.description: Delhi's most famous Mughal-style restaurant, operating since 1913 near Jama Masjid. Renowned for mutton burra kebab, nihari (slow-cooked mutton stew), and naan. A living culinary heritage institution.

places.name: Old Delhi Street Food Walk — Chandni Chowk
places.description: Chandni Chowk is India's most celebrated street food corridor. Must-try: paratha wali gali (stuffed parathas), jalebi from Oldman's Jalebi, chole bhature, dahi bhalla, and the legendary rabri at Natraj. Best experienced on foot with a guide.

places.name: Delhi Dilli Haat Craft Food Court
places.description: Government-run open-air craft market with rotating stalls from different Indian states. The food court offers authentic regional cuisine — Kashmiri wazwan, Rajasthani dal baati, Kerala fish curry, and North-East India specialities. Entry charged separately.
